hypothesis: When the first request after an engine start is a long prompt, q36c_mirror's first-forward reservation keeps almost all free memory for the prompt scratch, so the KV mirror past 8192 positions is taken from the expert tier (one 256 MiB block, about 78 experts out of the card for the rest of the process) and later decode slows. Sizing the first chunk before that mirror and keeping free only that chunk's scratch, the tier's staging room and a margin keeps every expert on the card, so decode after a long first prompt keeps its normal speed.
